# Tools categorically excluded from AnVIL harness runs.
#
# Purpose: as coverage widens from the current pinned list toward the full
# toolset, some tools can never produce a useful result here. Testing them
# spends a slot to manufacture a red cell every night, which trains everyone
# to ignore red cells. This file is the single place that decides which.
#
# Format: one entry per line, `#` starts a comment. Entries are matched as
# FIXED SUBSTRINGS against tool IDs (`grep -F -f`), so write them WITHOUT a
# version so they survive regeneration of scheduled-tool-ids.txt:
#
#     /repos/owner/name/tool_id/          <- version-independent, preferred
#     bare_tool_id                        <- for core tools with no repo path
#
# Bar for inclusion: the tool cannot pass in this deployment no matter what
# we fix on our side, AND that is a property of the tool rather than a bug we
# are chasing. A tool that is merely failing right now does NOT belong here -
# exclusion hides it. If in doubt leave it in and let it be red.
#
# Every entry states why and, where relevant, what would let it come back.
# Re-check this file whenever scheduled-tool-ids.txt is regenerated.


# --- Data managers -----------------------------------------------------
# Index/database builders do not test cleanly via galaxy-tool-test: they
# report a generic error with no per-test detail, or no report at all, while
# the underlying job (a real, often multi-hour index build) keeps running
# with nothing left to poll it - orphaned until GCP Batch's 24h
# max_run_duration kills it. Excluded as a category, not individually.
data_manager


# --- Broken test definition --------------------------------------------
# bg_uniq ships a single empty placeholder test:
#     <tests><test></test></tests>
# Its `input` param is required, galaxy-tool-test gives each case a fresh
# empty history, so submission is rejected with
# "Parameter 'input': specify a dataset of the required format / build".
# The tool itself works fine - verified, exit 0 on real tabular input. The
# toolshed repo has no linked source repository and exactly one revision
# (2013), so there is nowhere to send a fix.
# Revisit if a new revision with a real test is ever published.
/repos/bgruening/unique/bg_uniq/


# --- Container cannot start here ---------------------------------------
# mgnify_seqprep requests rz9082/seqprep:v1.2-mgnify-v5.0, a personal Docker
# Hub image with no /bin/bash. Galaxy's k8s runner launches containers with
# `command: [job_wrapper.shell]`, default /bin/bash, so the container never
# starts:
#     runc create failed: exec: "/bin/bash": stat /bin/bash: no such file
# Not fixable from the deployment: `shell` is a job_conf destination key and
# TPV has no `shell` attribute, so it cannot be set per-tool.
# Revisit if the tool moves to a biocontainer.
/repos/bgruening/mgnify_seqprep/


# --- Requirements that no biocontainer satisfies -----------------------
# These pin packages that were never built for conda, or ancient versions
# with no build. Container resolution returns nothing, they fall back to the
# Galaxy image, and fail on a missing binary. No image we could build helps:
# the package does not exist to install.
#
#   rpy 1.0.3   - the Python-2 predecessor of rpy2; no quay.io repo at all
#   R 2.11/2.15 - 2010-2012 era, no biocontainer build
#   MINE 1.0.1  - no quay.io repo
#   pass/gpass/beam/lps_tool - Galaxy-internal legacy binaries, never packaged
#
# Note these are NOT deprecated in the toolshed and still show ~2,500
# downloads each, so upstream has not signalled they are dead - but the
# packaging is. Only an upstream port (rpy -> rpy2) would revive them.
/repos/devteam/best_regression_subsets/
/repos/devteam/canonical_correlation_analysis/
/repos/devteam/correlation/cor2/
/repos/devteam/kernel_canonical_correlation_analysis/
/repos/devteam/kernel_principal_component_analysis/
/repos/devteam/lda_analysis/
/repos/devteam/linear_regression/
/repos/devteam/logistic_regression_vif/
/repos/devteam/mine/
/repos/devteam/partialr_square/
/repos/devteam/plot_from_lda/
/repos/devteam/principal_component_analysis/
/repos/devteam/rcve/
/repos/devteam/t_test_two_samples/
/repos/ethevenot/heatmap/Heatmap/
/repos/guru-ananda/karyotype_plot/
hgv_beam
hgv_gpass
hgv_lps
hgv_pass


# --- No test cases to run ----------------------------------------------
# These tools are installed and working - they simply ship zero tests, so
# Galaxy's tests_summary (the harness's tool source) never lists them and
# galaxy-tool-test has nothing to execute. Verified against a live instance:
# each is present in api/tools, and api/tools/<id>/test_data returns 0 cases
# (a control EMBOSS tool on the same instance returns 1). None of the seven
# produced a single result in the first 30 runs of the harness.
#
# Excluded rather than left in place: they cost a slot to produce nothing,
# and listing them here also keeps them out of any future regenerated list.
# Any of them comes back the moment its wrapper gains a test upstream.
#
#   isochore47, polydot77 - the only 2 of the 9 pinned EMBOSS tools without
#     tests; the other 7 test fine, so this is per-tool, not an emboss_5
#     packaging gap.
/repos/devteam/emboss_5/EMBOSS: isochore47/
/repos/devteam/emboss_5/EMBOSS: polydot77/
#
#   4 q2galaxy tools - the suite is installed and testable (140 qiime2 tools
#     in tests_summary, 10 of the 14 pinned ones run), so this is specific to
#     these wrappers, at every version they ship, not to QIIME2.
/repos/q2d2/qiime2__sample_classifier__predict_classification/
/repos/q2d2/qiime2__metadata__distance_matrix/
/repos/q2d2/qiime2__quality_control__evaluate_taxonomy/
/repos/q2d2/qiime2__rescript__evaluate_fit_classifier/
#
#   intermine - a Galaxy built-in with no tests. Built-ins are keyed
#     unversioned, so this is a bare id like the hgv_* entries above.
intermine

# --- Deliberately NOT excluded (recorded so nobody adds them) ----------
#
# Extract genomic DNA 1
#   Its history/custom-sequence branch is genuinely unfixable here (needs
#   faToTwoBit AND Galaxy's Python environment at once, and it is on
#   GALAXY_LIB_TOOLS_VERSIONED so container resolution is skipped). But 5 of
#   its 7 tests use the cached branch and now PASS. Excluding the tool would
#   discard that coverage to hide 2 known failures. The 2 remaining are
#   fixed by galaxyproject/galaxy#23411 once released.
#
# pretext_map
#   Fails on memory against the k8s destination's 4 GB ceiling. That is the
#   deployment's intended shape, so the failure is honest signal about what
#   this VM size can run. Exclude only if the resource shape becomes fixed
#   policy rather than something under review.
#
# amrfinderplus, gtdbtk_classify_wf
#   Empty reference-data dropdowns. Also broken on usegalaxy.org, so this is
#   an upstream galaxyproject/idc gap that may well be fixed. Leave visible.
#
